newsitem.title: FINLAND: Details of UPM, M-Serla deals.
newsitem.headline: Details of UPM, M-Serla deals.

text.p: Following are the details of a series of deals that Finnish forestry industry groups UPM-Kymmene Oy and Metsa-Serla Oy announced on Tuesday with chemical pulp producer Metsa-Botnia.
Metsa-Botnia is jointly owned by Metsa-Serla and Metsa-Serla's main owner the Metsaliitto group (53 percent), and UPM-Kymmene (47 percent).
UPM-Kymmene in a statement outlined the letter of intent for the deals, due for completion in the first quarter of 1997.
* UPM-Kymmene will sell its Simpele paperboard, paper and carton mills to Metsa-Serla and the Joutseno Pulp chemical pulp mill to Metsa-Botnia.
* Metsa-Botnia will immediately launch a development project worth 650 million markka at Joutseno Pulp.
* This will increase the mill's annual capacity by 30,000 tonnes to 350,000, company officials said.
* Metsa-Serla will sell the operations of Metsa-Sellu Oy (the Aanekoski pulp mill) to Metsa-Botnia.
* UPM-Kymmene will sell the wood supply operations of the Joutseno Pulp and Simpele mills to the cooperative Metsaliitto group of forestry owners.
* The value of the deal for UPM-Kymmene is about two billion markka, of which Metsa-Serla will pay nearly half in cash.
* UPM-Kymmene will invest the rest in Metsa-Botnia shares and in a shareholder loan to maintain the ownership structure and finance the investment in Joutseno Pulp.
* The arrangement will yield a sales profit of about 700 million markka to UPM-Kymmene.
* The deals are subject to approval by the respective boards of directors of the companies and competition authorities.
* The mills at Simpele and Joutseno Pulp had a combined turnover of two billion markka in 1995, with group internal sales accounting for 1.3 billion markka.
* The deals will increase UPM-Kymmene's self-supply of chemical pulp by about 50,000 tonnes a year.
